lines.text: A delivery robot asks its AI: is the path clear? The answer comes back: stop. Correct, but too late.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[0,3]. Original schematic braking example; no measured robot or physical safety claim.

lines.text: The problem is not how smart the AI is. It is when the answer arrives. The fix: let AI think, but keep the machine on time.
lines.source: Author's summary of the proposed architecture, repeated at the close.

lines.text: Inside the robot, a controller sends commands to the wheels many times a second. Waiting for the AI makes it miss commands. That is how the robot ran past the line.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[1,3]; lab-deadline-model.js blocking controller jobs. The visible beat is slowed for explanation.

lines.text: Three answers. Two arrive quickly. One takes longer. The machine cannot know which answer will hold it up.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[1,2]; lab-deadline-model.js synthetic latency. Three chosen examples, not a measured distribution or probability.

lines.text: Rule one: never wait. The AI works beside the controller. Every beat, the controller takes the latest finished answer.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[4,5]; lab-deadline-model.js async path. Adequate isolated controller resources assumed; contention addressed in open.

lines.text: But the latest answer can be old. Watch the box move. The answer still says the path is clear. It describes an older world.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[6]; original observation-snapshot illustration. An on-time action is not necessarily correct.

lines.text: Rule two: stamp each answer with the moment it saw the world. Too old? Throw it away.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[7]; lab-deadline-model.js age = startA - plan.at. Age includes inference time, not just time since completion.

lines.text: Rule three: always keep a simple backup the controller can do on time. Here, brake. The same moment again, and the robot stops before the line.
lines.source: scripts/narration.json determinism[7,8,11]; _pages/lab-determinism.md baseline caveat. Braking is a schematic example, not a verified safe controller.

lines.text: Those are the three rules. The open question: when large models and the controller share one chip, can we prove the clock still holds?
